# Enjoy a Long Stay on the Seafront of Marbella.

Enjoy the winter on the Costa del Sol by staying right by the sea at Puerto Azul Marbella, a highly valued option for senior tourism and long stays in Marbella.

### Why choose Puerto Azul for a long winter stay

- **Flat and Accessible Location:** Forget about the car. We are located on the seafront promenade, in a flat area with no hills, ideal for a morning walk.
- **24-Hour Security and Assistance:** Our reception is always open for anything you may need, giving you the peace of mind of a hotel with the freedom of a home.
- **Community and Peaceful Atmosphere:** A relaxed environment where you will share space with other guests looking for the same experience as you.

![Gallery 1](https://www.puertoazul.net/files-sbbasic/ba_apartpuertoazul_es/happy-senior-couple-strolling-along-seashore-spending-time-together-vacation-grey-haired-man-embracing-smiling-short-haired-woman-sunglasses-relationship-retirement-lifestyle-concept__1_.jpg?w=750&h=502.5)

### Details That Make the Difference

- **Fully Equipped Apartments:** Complete kitchens, housekeeping included and, above all, **beds designed for optimal rest**.
- **Guaranteed Accessibility:** Building with modern lifts and bathrooms with walk-in showers.
- **Connectivity:** High-speed Wi-Fi to stay in touch with family and international TV channels to feel at home.

![Gallery 2](https://www.puertoazul.net/files-sbbasic/ba_apartpuertoazul_es/casco_antiguo_de_marbella.png?w=750&h=502.5)

### Special Discounts for Long Stays

Save more the longer you stay with our winter offers:

- 7 nights or more → 5% discount
- 14 nights or more → 10% discount
- 21 nights or more → 15% discount
- 28 nights or more → 20% discount

[BOOK ON OUR OFFICIAL WEBSITE:](https://www.puertoazul.net/en/bookings)

![Your holidays are protected](https://www.puertoazul.net/files-sbbasic/ba_apartpuertoazul_es/img_2490-copy.jpg?w=750&h=502.5)

### Many of Our “Winter Guests” Return Year After Year

Every winter, we welcome many senior guests and long-stay travellers who return **season after season** to enjoy the tranquillity, the mild climate and the warm hospitality of Puerto Azul Marbella. Our “winter guests” find their second home by the sea here, and many **return for their stay** every year.

If you are looking for a place to feel at home during the colder months, **join our long-stay community** on the Costa del Sol.

- Arend, Netherlands: _"A clean apartment in a location close to the beach and the old town."_
- Eveline, Austria: _"Compared to last year: the Wi-Fi is faster and more stable, there are now warm duvets and a new air-conditioning unit (heating)."_
- Stephane, Canada: _"Impeccable reception. The location is ideal. The apartments are spacious and fully equipped with everything needed for cooking. The housekeeping staff are helpful and efficient. We loved our stay."_
- Seamus, Ireland: _"Returning guests. The staff are very friendly and helpful, as always. We will be back."_

Tripadvisor :

- [Monique and Brian, Ireland: _"A lovely holiday for walking and relaxing in the winter sun."_](https://www.tripadvisor.co/ShowUserReviews-g187439-d508274-r934116657-Puerto_Azul_Marbella-Marbella_Costa_del_Sol_Province_of_Malaga_Andalucia.html "(opens in new window)")

#### Frequently Asked Questions

###### Can I stay for several months during the winter?

Yes, Puerto Azul Marbella is open all year round and offers special conditions for extended stays during the winter season.

###### What services are included?

The accommodation includes a fully equipped apartment, WiFi 6 and LAN connection, daily housekeeping, 24-hour reception, a secure environment and access to 24-hour medical assistance.

###### Is it suitable for peaceful and safe long stays?

Yes, it is a highly valued option for guests seeking tranquillity, comfort and continuous assistance during extended stays.

![Gallery 4](https://www.puertoazul.net/files-sbbasic/ba_apartpuertoazul_es/view_from_front_sea_view.jpg?w=750&h=502.5)

### Marbella in Winter

Marbella in winter is the perfect destination for a peaceful and comfortable long stay. Thanks to its unique microclimate — with more than **320 days of sunshine** per year — nighttime temperatures rarely fall below 10ºC and daytime averages reach around 19ºC, allowing you to enjoy the outdoors even during the coolest months. Seafront walks, local gastronomy, hiking and cultural life without the summer crowds, with the **Old Town** within walking distance and close proximity to pharmacies and renowned health centres, make Marbella synonymous with well-being and quality of life all year round.

###### Your guide to a long term stay in Marbella

Marbella, located in the stunning Andalusia region of Spain, is a fantastic destination for long-term stays. With its picturesque coastline, vibrant culture, and mild climate, it’s perfect for those looking to immerse themselves in a beautiful environment. Whether you're considering month-to-month arrangements or an extended stay, Marbella offers a variety of furnished rentals that cater to different needs and budgets. From cozy apartments to luxurious villas, you can find the ideal spot for a memorable getaway.

###### Save on long term rentals in Marbella

For travelers planning an extended stay in Marbella, opting for long-term rentals can lead to significant savings and greater flexibility. Monthly rentals provide the comforts of home while allowing you to explore the region at your leisure. Discover a wide range of [discounted monthly rentals in Marbella](https://www.vrbo.com/search?regionId=5776) that are perfect for long-term living. And with properties offering free cancellation, you can book with confidence, knowing that you have options should your plans change.

###### Vacation Rentals for Digital Nomads and Remote Workers

If you're a digital nomad or remote worker, Marbella is an ideal location to blend work and leisure. The city offers numerous vacation rentals equipped with reliable WiFi, allowing you to stay connected while enjoying the sun. Explore [long-term rentals with great WiFi in Marbella](https://www.vrbo.com/search?regionId=5776&amenities_facilities_group=internet_available) that cater to your professional needs, making it easy to balance productivity with relaxation.

###### Pet-friendly accommodations in Marbella

Traveling with your furry friend? Marbella offers a variety of pet-friendly vacation rentals that make long-term stays comfortable for both you and your pet. With plenty of outdoor spaces and nearby beaches, you can enjoy quality time together. Check out [Marbella long-term rentals that welcome pets](https://www.vrbo.com/search?regionId=5776&house_rules_group=pets_allowed) for a truly inclusive experience during your stay.

###### Vacation rentals in Marbella with great kitchens

One of the joys of long-term travel is the ability to prepare your own meals. Marbella has many furnished rentals featuring well-equipped kitchens, perfect for cooking up local delicacies or enjoying a cozy dinner at home. Browse [furnished rentals with kitchens in Marbella](https://www.vrbo.com/search?regionId=5776&rooms_spaces_group=kitchen) to enhance your monthly stay and enjoy the comforts of home cooking.

###### No need to worry about parking

For those with vehicles, finding a rental with parking is essential when considering a long-term stay in Marbella. Fortunately, many monthly rentals come with secure parking options, making it easy for you to explore the stunning surroundings without the hassle of street parking. Discover [monthly rentals with parking in Marbella](https://www.vrbo.com/search?regionId=5776&amenities_facilities_group=parking) to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience during your stay.

###### Accessible vacation rentals in Marbella

Marbella also offers a range of wheelchair-accessible vacation rentals, ensuring that everyone can enjoy this beautiful destination. These accommodations are designed with comfort and accessibility in mind, making them perfect for long-term guests. Explore [Marbella's wheelchair-accessible rentals](https://www.vrbo.com/search?regionId=5776&accessibility_features_group=wheelchair_accessible) for a seamless experience tailored to your needs during your extended stay.

###### Marbella accommodations with a pool

What better way to experience the Mediterranean climate than staying in a rental with a pool? Whether you're enjoying a refreshing dip after a long day or lounging by the water, a pool adds a luxurious touch to your monthly stay. Browse [rentals with a pool in Marbella](https://www.vrbo.com/search?regionId=5776&amenities_facilities_group=pool) for the ultimate relaxation during your time in this stunning coastal city.

- Which top landmarks you shouldn't miss in Marbella?



You definitely want to check out the Old Town, also called the Casco Antiguo, which is full of charming whitewashed buildings and narrow streets. The Plaza de los Naranjos is a beautiful square in the heart of the Old Town. And don't forget to see the iconic Marbella Church, Iglesia de la Encarnación, with its beautiful bell tower.

- What are the best short term rentals in Marbella?





Among the short term rentals in Marbella, [Aqua Apartments Bellamar - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/59815754), [Marbella Village](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/39405576) and [Ona Marbella Inn](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15500256) are the most popular ones.

- What kind of weather can travelers expect in Marbella?



Marbella has a Mediterranean climate with warm, sunny summers and mild, wet winters. Expect average highs in the 80s during the summer and lows in the 50s during the winter. You'll get plenty of sunshine year-round!

- What are the best short term rentals with a pool in Marbella?





[Aqua Apartments Bellamar - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/59815754), [Ona Marbella Inn](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15500256) and [Ona Alanda Club Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15504796) are the best short term rentals with a pool in Marbella.

- Are there any famous stadiums or sports arenas in Marbella?



Marbella doesn't have any major stadiums or sports arenas. But there are many smaller sports venues and facilities, including the Marbella Football Center, a popular training ground for professional soccer teams.

- What are the best short term rentals with a jacuzzi in Marbella?





The best short term rentals with a jacuzzi in Marbella are [Aqua Apartments Bellamar - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/59815754), [Ona Alanda Club Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15504796) and [ÁTico En Apartahotel - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/1227671).

- What notable natural landmarks are near Marbella?



Marbella is right on the Costa del Sol, so you're surrounded by beautiful beaches. But for something different, head to the Sierra Blanca mountains, which are just a short drive away. You'll find hiking trails, stunning views, and even the famous La Concha mountain peak.

- What are the best short term rentals for families and kids in Marbella?





The best short term rentals for families and kids in Marbella are [Aqua Apartments Bellamar - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/59815754), [Marbella Village](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/39405576) and [Ona Marbella Inn](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15500256).

- What part of Marbella is ideal for finding lodging?



The most popular areas for lodging are the Golden Mile, which is known for its luxury hotels and villas, and Puerto Banús, a glamorous marina filled with shops, restaurants, and nightlife. But you can also find great options in the Old Town, which is more charming and traditional.

Thinking of Marbella rentals long term for your next move to the Costa del Sol? You’re in the right place. This in-depth guide from **Avida Estate** explains where to live, what it costs, how Spanish rental law works, and exactly how to secure the right apartment or villa for a long term rental in Marbella. Whether you want an apartment with sea views on the Golden Mile, a family home near schools in San Pedro de Alcántara, or a golf-side villa in Nueva Andalucía, we’ll help you make a confident, well-informed decision and rent in Marbella with ease.

## Best areas for Marbella rentals long term (neighborhood guide)

### Marbella Golden Mile and “golden mile” icons

![](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-26-1024x538.jpg)

The Marbella Golden Mile is the epitome of luxury and high-end living. Expect beautiful properties like Don Gonzalo or the Puente Romano area, many with 24 hour security, gardens and direct access to the beach promenade. You’ll see a mix of modern apartments, 3 bedroom apartments with 2 bathrooms, and villas with private terraces and jacuzzis. Proximity to restaurants and shops is excellent and the lifestyle is refined and convenient.

Best for:

- Tenants looking for luxury, brand new refurbishments and a great location.
- Those who want walking distance to beach clubs and fine dining.
- Longer-term residents who prefer a gated community with a communal pool and concierge services.

Typical homes:

- Apartment with sea views and private balcony.
- 3–4 bedrooms, ensuite bathrooms, secure parking and high-spec kitchen.
- Villas with private gardens, pool and sea or mountain views.

### Puerto Banús and Nueva Andalucía (Golf Valley)

![Nueva Andalucía, Costa del Sol](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-4-1024x538.jpg)

Nueva Andalucía surrounds world-class courses—Las Brisas, Aloha, and Los Naranjos de Marbella—offering the archetypal “golf lifestyle.” You can live in a serene enclave five minutes from the buzz of Puerto Banús/puerto banús, where you’ll find a marina, designer shops, and nightlife. Properties range from a bedroom apartment in a gated community with a communal swimming pool to modern villas with sea views.

Why consider it:

- Golf at your doorstep plus easy access to restaurants, gyms and schools.
- A balanced choice for couples and families who want proximity to Puerto Banús without living in it.
- Plenty of options available year-round, including partial sea views and mountain views.

### San Pedro de Alcántara and Guadalmina Baja

![San Pedro de Alcantara, Costa del Sol, Spain](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-7-1024x538.jpg)

San Pedro de Alcántara has Spanish town charm and a beautiful beach paseo. Guadalmina Baja has large plots, quiet streets and stately villas—perfect for a family home with private garden and pool. Schools and services are solid and proximity to Estepona and Marbella centre is very practical. Expect gated communities, 24 hour security in many enclaves and direct access to the beach in some properties.

Great for:

- Families who prioritise schools, parks and space.
- Tenants who want a calm, authentic and convenient base.

### Marbella East (East Marbella): Río Real, Bahía de Marbella, Los Monteros, Altos de Los Monteros

![Coast East Marbella](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-9-1024x538.jpg)

East Marbella is known for golden dunes and a peaceful coastline. Neighbourhoods like Río Real, Bahía de Marbella and Los Monteros are sought after areas for beach-first living while Altos de Los Monteros offers dramatic sea views. Expect brand new developments, modern apartments and townhouses with private terraces. Many homes here have partial sea views or panoramic sea views of the bay and coastline.

Best for:

- Beach lovers and health-focused lifestyles (dunes, paddle, beach clubs).
- Those who want quieter streets while staying close to central Marbella.

### Central Marbella town

![Marbella Old Town](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-15-1024x538.jpg)

Live car-free in central Marbella near Paseo Marítimo, Alameda and the Old Town. Buildings like Don Gonzalo and beachfront blocks put you steps from shops, restaurants, schools and clinics. Apartments are often refurbished to a modern style. Prices reflect the convenience and the fact you can do most errands on foot.

### Estepona and West Marbella “spillover”

![Estepona, Marbella, Andalucía, Spain](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-16-1024x538.jpg)

Estepona has boomed with modern complexes at a great price compared to central Marbella. It’s on the same coast, a short drive to San Pedro, with new builds and family-friendly amenities. If your budget is fixed but your wish list is long, Estepona often delivers more space and newer spec for the price.

Commute note:

- A-7 is the free coastal road; AP-7 is the tolled highway with faster travel in peak times.
- Málaga Airport to Marbella: around 40-50 minutes by car.
- School runs between Nueva Andalucía, San Pedro and East Marbella are practical with route planning.

## Property types and features for long term rent in Marbella

![Marbella Rentals Long Term](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-19-1024x538.jpg)

### Apartments

Apartments are the most common type of long term rental, from 1 bedroom to 3 bedroom apartments with 2 bathrooms. Many are in a gated community with 24 hour security, communal pool and gardens. An apartment with sea views will command a higher rent than one with partial sea views, especially on the Golden Mile or beachfront in East Marbella. Private terraces are common, often south/southwest facing for winter sun.

What to look for:

- Orientation (south/southwest is best for winter sun).
- Sound insulation and humidity control.
- Lift access and parking.
- Fiber internet available.

### Townhouses

Townhouses offer space and a home feel without the maintenance of a large villa. Most are in communities with pools and gardens—ideal for families who want shared amenities and safety. You’ll find them in Río Real, Bahía de Marbella, Nueva Andalucía and around San Pedro.

### Villas

Villas are the perfect home for privacy: private garden, swimming pool, often a jacuzzi and space for home offices. In Guadalmina Baja and the Golden Mile expect luxury builds and classic Andalusian style. In Altos de Los Monteros and the hills you’ll find brand new, luxury properties with panoramic views of the sea and La Concha.

Feature checklist:

- Heating and cooling (ducted AC, underfloor in newer homes).
- Security (alarm, cameras, 24 hour security in the community).
- Garage/driveway and storage.
- Garden and pool maintenance terms.

### Buildings and enclaves to know

- Don Gonzalo (central Marbella, luxury, beachside).
- Los Naranjos de Marbella (Nueva Andalucía, golf-side living).
- Río Real (golf + beach proximity), Bahía de Marbella, Los Monteros, Altos de Los Monteros.
- Guadalmina Baja (spacious, serene, close to San Pedro).

## Step-by-step: The Marbella long term rent process

![Marbella Rentals Long Term](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-1-1024x538.jpg)

1. Search and shortlist

- [Ask **Avida Estate**](https://avidaestate.com/contact/) for must-haves (gated community, sea views, walking distance to schools/shops, golf proximity) and nice-to-haves (jacuzzi, brand new, private terrace).
- Request video tours if you’re abroad.
- Prepare documents: passport, NIE (if available), proof of income, references.

2. Viewings

- Visit at different times to check noise, traffic and sun path on the private terrace.
- Test internet speeds, mobile signal and inspect for humidity.
- Confirm parking, storage and community rules (pets, renovations, use of communal swimming pool).

3. Application and documents

- Employed: contract + last 3 payslips + bank statements.
- Self-employed/company directors: last 6-12 months statements, tax returns.
- Non-residents: higher guarantees may be requested (e.g., aval bancario bank guarantee).

4. Offer and reservation

- Negotiate rent, start date, furniture, repainting, minor works.
- Pay a holding deposit to reserve (subject to contract).

5. Contract signing

- Long term residential contracts are governed by LAU (Uso de vivienda).
- Contract in Spanish; bilingual versions are common. Ensure you understand clauses on notice, updates and maintenance.

6. Move-in

- Inventory with photos/videos.
- Meter readings (electricity/water/gas).
- Receive keys, fobs, garage remotes and community rulebook.

**Avida Estate** manages each step, coordinating with landlords and communities to make your check-in smooth.

## Spanish rental law (LAU) essentials for long term rentals in Marbella

![](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-14-1024x538.jpg)

- Long term vs “11 months” myth: The contract type depends on the use. If the property is your habitual residence (uso de vivienda), LAU applies regardless of 11-month wording. “11 months” only fits a truly temporary use (e.g., work assignment).
- Duration and renewals: Standard is 1-year terms with tenant’s right to extend annually up to 5 years if the landlord is an individual, or up to 7 years if the landlord is a company. Laws can change; verify current rules at signing.
- Deposit and guarantees: The legal deposit (fianza) is typically one month’s rent for vivienda. In Andalucía it must be lodged with the regional authority (Junta de Andalucía via AVRA). Additional guarantees are common (extra months or aval bancario).
- Rent updates: Spain has applied temporary caps in recent years (e.g., 2–3%). A new Housing Index is planned to guide updates. Confirm the applicable cap/index at the time of signing.
- Early termination and notice: Tenants can usually leave after 6 months with 30 days’ written notice; compensation of up to one month per remaining year may apply if stated in contract.
- Who pays what: Landlords usually pay community fees and IBI (property tax). Tenants pay utilities and often the garbage tax (basura). Clarify in writing.
- Pets, subletting and works: Not all communities allow pets or alterations. Get permissions and scope of works approved in advance.

Helpful links:

- Junta de Andalucía (AVRA) deposit info: [https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/organismos/avra.html](https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/organismos/avra.html)
- Spanish LAU on BOE (in Spanish): [https://www.boe.es](https://www.boe.es/index.php?lang=en)

**Avida Estate** will guide you through these points and align the contract with current regulations.

## Family and lifestyle: Choosing your ideal home

![Marbella Lifestyle](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-1024x538.jpg)

Schools and education:

- Aloha College (Nueva Andalucía), Laude San Pedro (San Pedro de Alcántara), English International College (Marbella East), Swans, Laude Estepona, and others. These schools serve a thriving international community along the Costa del Sol.

Commute and daily convenience:

- Choose a home located close to your routine: schools, co-working, gyms, healthcare and your favorite restaurants and shops. Central Marbella and San Pedro help you live car-light; Nueva Andalucía is great if you play golf; East Marbella suits beach-first lifestyles.

Beach vs golf vs town:

- Beachfront gives unmatched convenience but at a premium.
- Golf-side homes are serene and green, with quick access to practice facilities.
- Town-center positions deliver walking distance ease and lively atmosphere.Quiet area vs nightlife:
- Peaceful? East Marbella, Guadalmina Baja and family areas in San Pedro.
- Lively? Puerto Banús and central Marbella have nightlife and dining, but noise checks during viewings.

## Where to find long term rentals in Marbella

![Marbella Rentals Long Term](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-18-1024x538.jpg)

- **Avida Estate** listings: We have carefully curated properties for long term rent across the Golden Mile, Nueva Andalucía, Río Real, Bahía de Marbella, Los Monteros, San Pedro de Alcántara, Guadalmina Baja and Puerto Banús. Expect vetted homes to the highest standards.
- Off-market and community networks: Many high demand homes circulate within building communities (e.g. Don Gonzalo, Los Naranjos de Marbella) before hitting portals. **Avida Estate** has access to these early.

## Tips to get the best long term rent

- Be flexible: Choose partial sea views over panoramic sea, or second-line over frontline beach to save 10-30% without sacrificing lifestyle.
- Time your move: September-May for more options and better terms.
- Strengthen your offer: Present complete documents, offer a longer term (e.g. 24-36 months) and propose minor improvements (fresh paint, small appliances).
- Check red flags: Verify ownership, ensure the property isn’t in community or tax arrears, confirm short-term letting is not allowed during your term and insist on a clear inventory.

## Moving-in checklist for long term rentals in Marbella

![Marbella Rentals Long Term](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-22-1024x538.jpg)

Before you sign:

- Passport/NIE, proof of income, contract in Spanish (with English translation if needed).
- Deposit receipt and proof of AVRA lodging.
- Community rules, pool schedules, pet policy.

Utilities and services:

- Electricity (Endesa or Iberdrola), water (Acosol), gas, fibre (Movistar, Orange, Digi).
- Air-con servicing and dehumidifiers in humid months.

Town hall and admin:

- Empadronamiento (municipal registration) at Marbella Town Hall: [https://www.marbella.es](https://www.marbella.es/)
- Health card, school enrollment and parking permits as applicable.Comfort and maintenance:
- Set recurring AC filter changes.
- Arrange gardener/pool service for villas.
- Log issues within the first 7 days with timestamped photos.

## Featured Snippet Q&A: Marbella long term rentals

![](https://avidaestate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Marbella-Rentals-Long-Term-11-1024x538.jpg)

How much is a 3 bedroom apartment long term in Marbella?

- A: 3,000–6,500 €/mo depending on area, property condition and sea views. Golden Mile can be +6,000 €/mo.

Is an 11 month contract legal for long term living?

- A: Not for habitual residence. If it’s your main home, LAU applies with standard renewals (5–7 years depending on landlord type).

What documents do I need to rent long term in Spain?

- Passport/NIE, proof of income (payslips or accounts), bank statements, references. Non-residents may need extra guarantees.

Who pays community fees and IBI on the Costa del Sol?

- Usually the landlord. Tenants pay utilities and often garbage tax—always confirm in the contract.

Can I register (empadronar) with a rental contract?

- Yes. Your contrato de arrendamiento plus utility/ID is usually enough at the town hall.
